## Mirket repository structure

Mirket is the principal repository/project. Its primary product is the distributable plugin under `plugins/mirket`, containing composable workflow skills, routing guidance, lifecycle hooks, metadata and references. An optional `memory/` subsystem provides project-specific memory-bank integration. The repository also contains a `website/` documentation and presentation application. The component map distinguishes the skill catalog from infrastructure that selects, reinforces, tests and distributes it.
- **Plugin and skill catalog:** `plugins/mirket` contains workflow modules at `skills/<lowercase-name>/SKILL.md`, each with YAML front matter and `agents/openai.yaml`; supporting material is in `references/`. The website includes a pixel meerkat in the hero panel.
- **Website:** `website/` contains a locally implemented static-export site that presents the Mirket workflow, skill guide and installation flow, with animated diagrams. It is a presentation and documentation surface built from the plugin documentation and routing guidance, rather than another workflow subsystem.
- **Metadata and distribution:** `plugin.json`, README, display metadata, icon and manifests. `plugin.json` is the implementation descriptor; README is the lean public quick start, while `CONTRIBUTING.md` contains maintainer guidance.
- **Routing:** `references/routing.md` maps requests to owner skills and records boundaries, including Design/Imagine, Distill/Author, Curate and compact-plan rules. The active routing convention combines this guide with each packaged skill's trigger description; routing is guidance, not guaranteed enforcement.
- **Hooks:** `plugins/mirket/hooks` integrates prompt, stop, pre-tool-use and cleanup behavior. `distill.py` supplies communication guidance; `cleanup.py` handles cleanup, commit acknowledgment and staged `.work/` inspection.
- **Workspace:** `.work/` stores task and planning state. Reusable handoffs go in `.work/briefs/`, private architectural notes and drafts in ignored `.work/decisions/`, and recovery material in `.work/recover/`.
- **Checks:** Python `unittest` covers hooks, installation and project routing. Plugin, memory, catalog and formatting checks have passed at times, but these do not establish live host behavior.

- **Documentation site content pipeline:** The Mirket website uses repository Markdown as the shared source for GitHub and the site. It renders the repository guide on documentation routes. The site provides copyable agent prompts and manual installation commands for Codex and Claude Code, while the README includes static versions of the diagrams and shareable diagram stills.

- **Website implementation and interaction surface:** The website is a source-backed static-export Next.js presentation layer implemented as a local static export, with generated output in `website/out`. Pages live under `app/`, reusable UI under `components/`, and build-time loading and discovery under `lib/`. `lib/content.ts` reads repository Markdown and packaged skill YAML; `RepoMarkdown.tsx` maps repository links to local documentation routes or GitHub; `lib/discovery.ts` supplies a shared `PageInfo` model for canonical paths, metadata and public-page discovery. It generates skill documentation and adjacent-skill navigation for the 25-skill catalog, currently describing 28 indexable pages, and publishes structured metadata, sitemap, robots, `llms.txt` and social images. Responsive workflow diagrams support reduced-motion static presentation.

- **Plugin distribution descriptors:** Mirket is distributed as one collection of 25 composable workflows. Marketplace descriptors point to `plugins/mirket`, whose version-0.4.0 metadata includes the portable Codex manifest (`plugin.json`), the Claude manifest (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`), the icon, skill files, Codex display metadata and shared references.

- **Packaging and host entry points:** Mirket is a skill plugin for Codex and Claude Code. The root marketplace manifests `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` both resolve to `plugins/mirket/`, which is the shared package source containing host-specific descriptors, Markdown skills, YAML display metadata, references and the icon. Mirket's native skills catalog uses the `mirket` namespace and is distributed through a marketplace with remote setup and local workspace rules. JSON manifests handle packaging and hook registration.

- **Canonical skill package model:** A skill is a named Markdown workflow whose directory name is its stable lowercase slug. `SKILL.md` front matter defines its trigger and description, `agents/openai.yaml` supplies display metadata, and References provide supplemental guidance. Both supported agent hosts consume this same package; the website reads it as source content rather than maintaining a second catalog.

- **Website architecture:** Within `website/`, pages live under `app/`, reusable UI components under `components/`, and build-time content loading under `lib/`. The site loader accepts lowercase skill slugs containing digits and hyphens, reads each accepted directory's Markdown and YAML, and sorts the discovered skills by display name.

- **Validation entry points:** Repository checks run with `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests` and memory checks with `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s memory`. Coverage includes lifecycle continuation, staged-path protection, project and worktree identity, concurrent registry writes, installer rollback and diagnostic session counts.

- **Routing discoverability:** In the current working tree, `hooks/distill.py` emits the one-owner rule and the exact path to `plugins/mirket/references/Routing.md` at SessionStart, and key packaged skills link to that guide. This corrects the earlier discoverability gap for working-tree audits; live activation, released behavior and semantic routing remain unverified.

- **Repository documentation and checks:** `docs/` contains the main guide, workflow diagrams and decision records; `README.md` introduces installation and features, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents contributor checks. `tests/` covers hooks, distribution wiring, manifest and marketplace integrity, Markdown links and behavioral-fixture preparation, while `memory/test_*.py` covers the optional memory integration.

## Core workflow skills

The skills form a routed workflow rather than independent subsystems. Mirket assigns one skill responsibility for each outcome, with supporting skills returning evidence to that owner. The router selects an owner; Orchestrate coordinates multi-step work; Plan and Architect establish structure and decisions; implementation, quality, communication and handoff skills operate within that scope.

- **Adapt:** recovers missing or stale context through read-only investigation, rechecks decision-affecting facts and proceeds directly when an authorized fix is clear.
- **Architect:** handles consequential technical choices, gathers evidence, uses diagrams when useful, records settled ADRs in the project's established `docs/decisions/` location (initializing it when no convention exists), and escalates material product, cost, security or operational impacts. Private notes and drafts remain in `.work/decisions/`.
- **Audit:** performs scoped, read-only review; distinguishes defects, risks and improvements, reports exclusions and fixes only when authorized.
- **Author:** owns documents, substantive product copy and issue triage. Routine replies belong to Distill.
- **Brief:** creates actionable handoffs containing purpose, result, next action, boundaries and essential evidence; reusable or requested handoffs are stored in `.work/briefs/`.
- **Clean:** performs scoped cleanup and recovery, preserves uncertain files, corrects stale guidance only with evidence and makes verified recovery copies before authorized removal.
- **Critique:** assesses quality during implementation and before delivery, requiring evidence for visual/performance claims and reporting unverified areas.
- **Curate:** compares options rather than conducting general research; scales research to stakes, uncertainty and cost, discloses evidence gaps and gives conditional recommendations when needed.
- **Design:** owns the design-director guide and design references for product UI, websites, illustration, brand systems, motion, slides and generative artwork. It is one skill at `plugins/mirket/skills/design/SKILL.md` with ten selectable references, including `motion-and-gestures.md`; it is not a set of mandatory `design-*` stage skills. The motion reference covers timing, interruption, reduced motion, alternate controls and safe removal. Design's handoffs are defined jointly with the shared routing guide and the Imagine and Critique skills.
- **Imagine:** receives generated interface references from Design; posters, identity references remain Design-owned.
- **Distill:** owns routine replies and communication guidance, emphasizing findings, changes, blockers, evidence and material limitations. The revised guidance directs authorized work to happen before routine narration, skips unnecessary narration, leads with verified results and applies concise factual communication at session start and on every prompt. At turn end it shares Clean's existing review pass rather than requesting a separate continuation. Author owns substantive written work.
- **Equip:** governs changes to tools, workflows or the environment; such changes require human agreement unless specifically authorized. It challenges materially poor choices even when they work by identifying excess cost, risk, constraints, inefficiency or data-correctness problems; it compares staying, adjusting, piloting or switching against adoption, migration, compatibility, retraining and ongoing ownership costs. Its 13 approved discussion scenarios are kept in a separate reference, including cases where keeping the current choice is best, and authorized setup includes a representative task check.
- **Focus:** belongs to the engineering/workflow-quality family; no narrower responsibility is established in the retrieved history.
- **Orchestrate:** is the top-level coordinator and sole delegator. It assigns work, reviews evidence, reassigns defective work, matches capability to task needs and continues inline when delegation is unavailable. After workers return ownership, it permits bounded root integration fixes while retaining independent review when required. Clear execution authorization is respected; an unapproved plan is not treated as approval. Substantial work normally uses Plan and resolves material decisions, with stronger approval gates when explicitly required.
- **Plan:** handles substantial work or explicit planning requests, records routine adjustments, preserves planning files and requires independent review for substantial plans, reporting when unavailable. It asks for confirmation only when authorization, outcomes or product decisions change.
- **Preflight, Refactor and Test:** cover readiness, behavior-preserving engineering changes and validation. Meaningful behavior or regression risk warrants tests or focused characterization checks; blocked required checks are reported as unverified.
- **Debug:** handles debugging-oriented engineering work; no narrower algorithm or file boundary is recorded.
- **Sleep:** safely pauses and resumes task-owned work, captures essential state, stops task-owned agents, records active work and avoids unnecessary handoffs.

- **Recent routing refinement:** Imagine's picker treats implementation as optional; when skill ownership is unclear, repository instructions direct agents to `references/routing.md`. Supplied-mockup routing remains Design-owned.

- **Equip:** guides authorized tool selection, acquisition and first verification while preserving human control. It challenges materially poor choices even when they work by identifying excess cost, risk, constraints, inefficiency or data-correctness problems; it compares staying, adjusting, piloting or switching against adoption cost and evidence.

- **Catalog boundary:** The expanded catalog now has explicit ownership for security, versioned release preparation, persistent-state migration, rollout and service health/recovery through Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy and Operate. Focus reviews the shipped outcome. The catalog remains stronger from deciding and building through verification than as a substitute for host- or organization-specific production systems.

- **Product-lifecycle skills:** The 25-workflow catalog adds distinct ownership for lifecycle work: **Secure** handles security and privacy; **Release** prepares versioned releases; **Migrate** changes persistent state; **Deploy** rolls releases out; and **Operate** maintains service health and recovery. **Focus** also reviews the shipped outcome. A representative lifecycle is Release → Deploy → Operate → Focus, with Secure and Migrate contributing where their ownership applies.

## Lifecycle and protection subsystem

The lifecycle subsystem connects routed skills to repository events and is distinct from the skills.

- **Prompt routing:** may request Distill or another skill and provide communication guidance, but cannot guarantee compliance. In the current working tree, `UserPromptSubmit` and SessionStart guidance surface the one-owner rule and the exact routing-guide path; released and live behavior remain unverified.
- **Host protocol:** Lifecycle hooks are scripts invoked by the host. The plugin descriptor registers `hooks/hooks.json`; host events invoke `distill.py` or `cleanup.py`, and the scripts return JSON for the host to interpret. Live host behavior and released behavior remain unverified.
- **Cleanup and commit protection:** `cleanup.py` handles malformed input, unsafe or unacknowledged commits, cleanup review and staged `.work/` inspection. Current hardening requires a deterministic absolute `git -C` target for guarded commits, keeps `git commit --dry-run` read-only, and blocks when the target index cannot be inspected. Earlier commands must not alter that target.
- **Enforcement scope:** recognized commit commands must run separately from other shell commands so earlier commands cannot alter the inspected index. Hooks guard a defined subset of direct agent-shell Git commits; they are workflow guardrails, not a complete shell parser or security boundary, and their live behavior depends on host support and hook trust.

- **Runtime constraints and input handling:** Mirket uses lightweight Python hooks for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and Bash PreToolUse events. Hook commands run in isolated Python mode with five-second manifest timeouts; sampled hooks consume and emit JSON, handle malformed input without tracebacks, ignore unsupported events, and cleanup parses only a bounded literal shell-command subset rather than evaluating shell syntax.

## Optional Mirket memory subsystem

The `memory/` area is an optional, separate project-and-bank integration. It is an internal repository subsystem, not part of the workflow catalog. Its project registry resolves canonical repository identities, shares a bank across subdirectories and linked worktrees, gives unmapped roots unique isolated identities, preserves compatible mappings and legacy banks, and rejects conflicting aliases or duplicate banks. A shared bank resolver is used by the integration's hooks, interactive memory path, survey adapter and backfill routing; the adapter refuses writes when the resolved bank differs and can recover durable session-to-project bindings from verified transcript metadata. Eligible history is reconciled non-destructively. Reproducible wiring and fast page-first injection provide recall with source recall for fresh facts. `memory/doctor.py` diagnoses coverage and freshness, while live readiness, coverage and freshness are checked separately.

Mirket is not itself a memory store; the optional integration keeps memory isolated by project. Linked worktrees resolve to their project's bank, unrelated repositories with the same name are rejected, compatible mappings are preserved, conflicting aliases and duplicate banks are rejected, and unmapped roots receive unique isolated identities.

- **Canonical routing:** The registry uses the canonical project directory as the routing unit: Git subdirectories and linked worktrees resolve to the same main project, while non-Git sessions retain their original directory. A stable bank comes from that canonical path or an existing explicit mapping, so repository basenames alone cannot merge unrelated projects.

- **Installation and diagnostics:** The optional installer supports read-only preflight, fresh installation and rewiring recognized installations while preserving unrelated configuration and saving recovery copies. It installs project-specific bank routing, keeps background surveys in the same bank and enables page-first injection; `doctor.py` reports routing, daemon health, conversation coverage, survey findings, page freshness and targeted recall as separate diagnostics. Runtime state and memory remain outside the repository.

- **Consistency and session continuity:** The adapted worker requires all four survey findings before completing a survey. Durable session-to-project bindings can be recovered from verified transcript metadata when a temporary marker is absent.

- **Common launcher:** `memory/install.py` wires `project_registry.py` as the shared launcher for Codex hooks and MCP, while validating existing configuration, preserving unrelated settings and saving recovery copies before rewiring.

## Dependency and control relationships

- Catalog and skill files provide workflow behavior; routing references select owners and define boundaries.
- Orchestrate coordinates specialized workers and retains root-level review. Plan supplies work records and gates; Architect handles consequential decisions; Brief transfers context; Sleep pauses work; Clean protects workspace state.
- Curate, Design, Imagine, Author and Distill define option, design and communication ownership: Design owns most design references, Imagine receives generated interface references, Distill owns routine replies and Author owns substantive writing and issue triage.
- Audit, Critique, Preflight, Refactor and Test provide review and verification around implementation.
- Hooks reinforce routing and protect lifecycle/workspace state but do not guarantee skill enforcement.
- Memory is orthogonal to the catalog and supplies project-isolated capture and recall. Consistent identity resolution is required across hooks, interactive sessions, surveys, backfill, subdirectories and linked worktrees.

- Within the optional memory subsystem, the project registry and bank resolver are the shared authority for hook, interactive and survey consumers; session-binding recovery supports continuity, page-first injection supports recall, and the doctor checks coverage and freshness. This subsystem remains orthogonal to the workflow catalog.

- **Website relationship:** The `website/` application is Mirket's documentation and distribution surface. It consumes repository Markdown as a shared source for GitHub and the site, rendering the repository guide on documentation routes. Each packaged `SKILL.md` powers a skill detail page; packaged skill metadata powers homepage cards, while the Markdown documentation provides shared sidebar and section navigation plus breadcrumbs and previous/next links. It presents installation guidance, including copyable agent prompts and manual commands; it does not select or execute skills.

- **Workflow visualization data:** `website/data/workflows.json` is separate from the packaged skill catalog. It supplies the ordered stages, labels and glyphs for the browser workflow player and for the Node-generated SVG diagrams checked into `docs/diagrams/`; the guide and generated diagrams therefore document or visualize workflows without becoming additional skills.

## Repository state and implementation caveats

The repository moved from `/Users/nazmi/Desktop/skills` to `~/Projects/skills` on November 9, 2026. The old checkout was removed while Git history was preserved in `.work/recover/2026-11-09-mirket-relocation/retired-reference.bundle`; the moved checkout retained memory-bank mapping and the standalone Hindsight skill.

Historical revisions were sometimes reported as implemented while remaining uncommitted, uninstalled or behaviorally untested, including Author, Curate, Adapt, Audit, Critique, Orchestrate and portions of lifecycle-hook work. Mirket 0.2.1 was subsequently audited, repaired and published, with its installed copy refreshed. Static and synthetic checks remain distinct from live host behavior, and hook behavior still depends on host support and hook trust.

The November 10, 2026 Design rewrite passed all 53 repository tests, with all ten Design references reachable. Earlier Mirket 0.2.0/0.2.1 publication and installation checks remain dated validation history; the current source manifests identify Mirket 0.4.0 with 25 workflows. Repository, packaging and catalog checks validate source and distribution behavior, while individual live hook behaviors still require separate host verification.

After workers hand ownership back, the root may make bounded integration fixes while retaining independent review when required. The root inspects results and evidence according to risk, sends defective work back for correction or reassignment, and rechecks the result. **Mirket's repository structure, naming, and Python style:** Mirket organizes skills under `plugins/mirket/skills/<lowercase-name>/SKILL.md`; a skill directory's lowercase name is its stable slug, `SKILL.md` contains YAML front matter and Markdown workflow content, `agents/openai.yaml` supplies Codex display metadata, and supplemental guidance lives in `references/` directories. Reference filenames use PascalCase; ordinary Markdown files use PascalCase except conventional names such as `SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md`; Python modules and tests use snake_case; React components use PascalCase filenames, with Next App Router `page.tsx` and `route.ts` entry points. Shared references are stored in `plugins/mirket/references/`, while narrower material remains colocated with its skill. Behavioral fixtures initially record an unverified result; creating one is not evidence that a host or model passed it. **Mirket's release validation pattern:** The Mirket 0.2.0 publication passed 23 plugin tests and 30 memory tests, 53 repository tests in total; all ten Design references were reachable and all 28 requested sources were covered. Mirket 0.2.1 later passed all 53 repository tests, a static website build, and browser smoke checks for installer layout and documentation links, and was committed, published, and pushed to `main`; its installed copy was refreshed. A later audit-fix run passed all 63 tests, the static site build, and SEO checks. Package-level, browser, and repository checks remain distinct from live behavioral verification: the Design rewrite and live skill selection in Codex and Claude Code were not tested in the earlier review, and package or synthetic checks are not presented as proof of live host behavior. The 0.2.1 audit and repair reduced prompt-hook text from 3,517 to 272 characters and active workflow entrypoints by 84%, removed duplicate ledgers and approval gates, resolved conflicting rules, corrected plan recovery and marker reads, and fixed Codex patch delivery to the Design detector.

**Mirket's routing-guidance pattern:** Compact plans record authorization in their own `Agreement` section. Imagine's picker makes implementation optional, and Codex and Claude instructions direct ambiguous skill ownership to the shared routing guide.

**Mirket's website structure, visual, and accessibility pattern:** The project website lives under `website` and produces a static export. The Mirket skills website uses a compact retro-styled hero description, a stable installer viewport, consistent navigation across the Markdown guide, memory guide, and skill pages, and the normal Mirket logo in the header, footer, and favicon. Its homepage places compact workflow diagrams titled **How it Works** below the installer, without the old introductory copy. The pixel meerkat mascot preserves the logo's black-and-cream side profile and face markings, responds to hero-link hover and focus, hops and waves after **Say hello**, and winks periodically while respecting the site-wide reduced-motion preference. Reduced motion follows the system setting rather than relying on individual animation controls; the mascot remains still and uses a still greeting pose with a heart when reduced motion is enabled. The interaction was checked across desktop, mobile, keyboard controls, and reduced-motion behavior.

**Mirket's website validation pattern:** Website changes are validated with a production-build check plus desktop and mobile layout checks, including the stable installer viewport, installation switching, command copying, reduced-motion behavior, keyboard access to desktop skill articles, the documentation skip link and mobile skill menu, and widths down to 320px. The mascot interaction was checked across desktop, mobile, keyboard controls, and reduced-motion behavior; the wink plays once and returns to the open-eye sprite, while the system reduced-motion preference keeps the sprite still. The homepage diagrams have no individual playback controls or footer motion setting; animations honor the browser/system reduced-motion preference. The static website build and desktop/mobile checks passed.

**Mirket's state and failure-handling pattern:** The project registry validates state under a POSIX file lock, preserves unrelated settings, rejects conflicting routing and unrecognized runtime changes, and atomically replaces JSON; it reports skipped isolation operations on stderr. Active requests use the canonical main Git project identity, while legacy mapping keys are resolved; linked-worktree behavior must avoid creating a fresh bank that splits memory from the existing project bank, by canonicalizing the mapping or explicitly rejecting it. The installer validates existing configuration before rewiring it, saves recovery copies for rollback, and stops before upstream installation when prerequisites or existing configuration are unsuitable, rather than proceeding with an unsafe or incompatible setup. Memory reliability work preserves working-tree revisions, configuration, canonical bank migration, effective diagnostics, freshness and recovery checks, and reports that instantaneous consistency cannot be guaranteed.

**Mirket's documentation and website-source pattern:** Packaged skill metadata powers homepage cards, and each `SKILL.md` powers a skill detail page. Documentation provides shared navigation with section links, a skill index, links to adjacent skills, and skill-page breadcrumbs plus previous/next links. Static versions of the workflow diagrams are generated for the README. Mirket's public-facing documentation also emphasizes source-backed content, search discoverability, and social previews rather than maintaining separate hand-written site copies.

**Mirket's skill-discovery and source-of-truth pattern:** A Mirket skill is a named Markdown workflow whose `SKILL.md` front matter defines its trigger and description. The website loader accepts lowercase skill slugs containing digits and hyphens, reads each accepted directory's Markdown and YAML, and sorts skills by display name. Both Codex and Claude Code consume the same package, and the website treats packaged skills as source content rather than maintaining a separate skill catalog.

**Mirket's website code structure and source-driven metadata:** The public site is a static Next.js application under `website/`; pages live under `app/`, reusable UI components under `components/`, and build-time content loading under `lib/`. The shared `PageInfo` model in `lib/discovery.ts` contains canonical paths, titles, descriptions, and social-card fields; Next metadata, structured data, and discovery lists are derived from that model. App Router pages generate the home catalog, documentation overview, and one route per skill, while skill routes are constrained to generated `/docs/skills/<slug>/` pages so unknown slugs do not create arbitrary dynamic pages. At build time, the loader reads packaged skill sources, including display metadata; internal Markdown links are mapped to site routes or GitHub. The workflow diagram is maintained separately from the packaged skill catalog, with ordered stages, labels, and glyphs sourced from `workflows.json`.

**Mirket's generated-asset and contribution conventions:** Checked-in SVG workflow diagrams are regenerated with `npm run docs:diagrams` after shared diagram data changes. Website checks include the diagram generation check, static build, and `seo:check`; the discovery checker parses exported HTML, metadata, structured data, and PNG headers and dimensions. `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires the root and packaged MIT license notices to remain aligned, requires original native skill guidance based on Mirket's requirements and observed behavior rather than external skills, prompts, or workflow guides, and documents the contributor checks.

**Mirket's lifecycle-hook responsibility and failure-handling pattern:** Lifecycle hooks are Python 3.8+ scripts invoked by the host and return JSON for host interpretation. They provide prompt guidance, remind the agent about Distill and Clean, and guard a defined subset of direct agent-shell Git commits; they do not perform cleanup themselves. UserPromptSubmit directs the agent toward Distill and reminds it about Clean. The cleanup hook is neutral by default and activates the extra final review only when `MIRKET_FINAL_REVIEW=1`; a neutral result does not itself establish that an optional review ran. Guarded commit inspection requires an absolute `git -C` target, while read-only previews remain non-mutating. Cleanup explicitly diagnoses malformed or unsupported input and denies recognized commit shapes that it cannot inspect safely. Live behavior remains dependent on host support and hook trust.

Audits of Mirket distinguish pre-existing staged and unstaged working-tree revisions from released or installed state: the surveyed audit changes were not to be described as released or installed merely because local tests, the website build, SEO checks, or discovery checks passed.

Imagine obtains explicit agreement on detailed image briefs while reusing prior approval. Preflight, Refactor, and Test add tests for meaningful behavior or regression risk, use focused characterization checks when needed, and report blocked required checks as unverified while running other relevant checks. Debug continues with available evidence when a specialist is unavailable while disclosing material gaps, fixes bugs within the requested scope, and diagnoses only when asked. Design asks before unresolved consequential design or business-rule decisions and stops redesigns until the existing interface is visible; generated interface references route to Imagine, while posters, identity references, and supplied mockups retain their existing Design routes. Brief and Orchestrate pause only for discrepancies relevant to the assignment, rather than for every stale-context difference.

**Mirket's published Design workflow pattern:** In Mirket 0.2.0, Design is one self-contained skill at `plugins/mirket/skills/design/SKILL.md` with ten selectable references, including motion and gestures. It covers product UI, websites, illustration, brand systems, motion, slides, and generative artwork, and uses the shared routing guide plus Imagine and Critique for handoffs. The earlier five-stage `design-*` workflow is historical and is not part of the published package; those stages are not mandatory modules.

The two root marketplace manifests resolve to the shared `plugins/mirket/` package directory, which contains host-specific descriptors, skills, metadata, references, and an icon. Mirket code uses small named functions, `pathlib`, explicit entry points, and standard-library Python modules; JSON manifests handle packaging and hook registration.

Fixtures cover continuation loops, staged paths, same-name unrelated projects, nested projects, aliases, linked worktrees, concurrent registry writes, installer rollback, and diagnostic session counts. Package-wiring tests compare host manifests with marketplace targets and validate exact-case paths, Markdown links, and anchors. Behavioral fixtures initially record an unverified result; creating one is not evidence that a host or model passed it. Mirket documents separate synthetic package checks from live host installation and behavioral verification, so passing package or synthetic checks is not presented as proof of live host behavior.

The homepage diagrams have no individual playback controls or footer motion setting; animations honor the browser/system reduced-motion preference. The static website build and desktop/mobile checks passed.

Active requests use the canonical main Git project identity, while legacy mapping keys are resolved; linked-worktree behavior must avoid creating a fresh bank that splits memory from the existing project bank, by canonicalizing the mapping or explicitly rejecting it. The installer validates existing configuration before rewiring it, saves recovery copies for rollback, and stops before upstream installation when prerequisites or existing configuration are unsuitable, rather than proceeding with an unsafe or incompatible setup. Memory reliability work preserves working-tree revisions, configuration, canonical bank migration, effective diagnostics, freshness and recovery checks, and reports that instantaneous consistency cannot be guaranteed.

**Mirket's documentation and website-source pattern:** Packaged skill metadata powers homepage cards, and each `SKILL.md` powers a skill detail page. Documentation provides shared navigation with section links, a skill index, links to adjacent skills, and skill-page breadcrumbs plus previous/next links. Static versions of the workflow diagrams are generated for the README. Mirket's public-facing documentation also emphasizes source-backed content, search discoverability, and social previews rather than maintaining separate hand-written site copies.

**Mirket's skill-discovery and source-of-truth pattern:** A Mirket skill is a named Markdown workflow whose `SKILL.md` front matter defines its trigger and description. The website loader accepts lowercase skill slugs containing digits and hyphens, reads each accepted directory's Markdown and YAML, and sorts skills by display name. Both Codex and Claude Code consume the same package, and the website treats packaged skills as source content rather than maintaining a separate skill catalog.

## Available project vocabulary

The project-attributed vocabulary identified across the history centers on the **Mirket** repository and its skill-based agent workflow. Mirket is the catalog namespace and primary plugin offering: a distributable collection of **25 composable agent workflows** for Codex and Claude Code, covering project orientation, architecture, product framing, planning, implementation, security, migration, release, deployment, operations, debugging, testing, audits, design, writing, handoffs, and coordination. Its core abstractions are named skills, routing, orchestration, delegation, persistent plans, review, feedback, memory continuity, and distribution hooks. The repository also contains the **Mirket website**, a separate static documentation and discovery project intended to make the plugin easier to understand and use; its implementation includes repository-sourced content, workflow diagrams, and a compact skill index.

Project-attributed concepts and entities recorded are:

Project-attributed concepts and entities recorded are:
- **Mirket** — the project's catalog namespace and primary plugin offering.
- **Mirket plugin** — the distributable collection of composable agent workflows, references, metadata, branding, and lifecycle integrations. Version **0.4.0** documents **25 workflows**. Historical catalog views include **43 skills** and a relationship model with **20 current skills**, including **18 parent skills** linked to upstream guidance; these are distinct historical or catalog views, not interchangeable current counts.
- **Mirket skill catalog** — the project's reusable capability catalog. A **skill** is a named, focused agent workflow defined in `plugins/mirket/skills/<lowercase-name>/SKILL.md`; skills are connected by shared routing references and direct references in their definitions. The packaged skill directories are the source of truth consumed by the website.
- **Skill package structure** — each Mirket skill has YAML front matter and an `agents/openai.yaml` display/configuration file, with optional supporting material in a skill's `references/` directory.
- **pick-skills** — the earlier/main routing skill for selecting the appropriate skill set and routing requests to owners such as Adapt, Plan, Debug, Test, and Design. The active package's current routing convention is instead defined by `plugins/mirket/references/routing.md` together with each packaged skill's trigger description; the active package contains no `pick-skills` skill file.
- **resolve-intent** — clarifies the user's request before work is assigned.
- **Plan** — creates persistent, explicit plans for substantial work or explicit planning requests, records routine technical adjustments, and uses three `.work` records for substantial work while permitting a compact plan for small work.
- **Execution authorization and written-plan approval** — distinct planning concepts. Substantial implementation normally requires using Plan, resolving material decisions, and confirming authorization to execute; clear existing execution authorization remains valid without treating an unapproved written plan as approved. Stronger approval gates still apply when the request is for a plan or approval is otherwise required.
- **review-plan** — spawns an independent reviewer for substantial plans and reports when independent review is unavailable.
- **delegate** — assigns work to subagents with task-appropriate reasoning effort; it is governed by Orchestrate rather than allowing arbitrary nested delegation.
- **get-feedback** — requires user feedback on partial implementations before completing the full implementation.
- **Orchestrate** — the coordinating skill and delegation policy. The root agent is the sole delegator; subagents cannot create or manage further subagents. Substantial work means work with consequential risk, unresolved decisions, or multiple dependent stages. Orchestrate requires Plan and the applicable execution-authorization conditions before delegating substantial implementation, permits direct delegation of small clearly scoped tasks, matches model capability and cost to determinism, creativity, risk, and ambiguity, inspects delegated results according to risk, assigns corrections, and remains accountable for the final result. If delegation is unavailable, it continues inline with a clear disclosure and preserves independent-review requirements.
- **Root agent and subagents** — Mirket's execution roles: the root agent coordinates, delegates, reviews, and remains accountable; subagents perform delegated work without further delegation authority.
- **Distill and Author** — response-routing skills. Since 10 November 2026, Distill handles routine replies, while Author is reserved for documents, substantive copy, and issue triage.
- **Architect** — the skill for consequential technical choices in new or existing systems. It escalates decisions with material product, cost, security, or operational impact while leaving routine decisions within existing authorization.
- **Critique** — the assessment workflow used during implementation when useful and before delivery when quality needs judgment. It selects risk-relevant lenses, reports evidence gaps, fixes and rechecks issues within scope, and escalates material taste, product-direction, or unresolved performance concerns.
- **Adapt** — uses relevant authorized memory while checking whether it is stale enough to affect a decision.
- **Curate** — scales research to the decision and expands a known comparison only when the additional research is material and in scope.
- **Brief** — preserves essential facts and identifies inaccessible sources when an important source cannot be consulted.
- **Equip** — governs changes to tools or workflows and requires human agreement for those changes.
- **Preflight, Refactor, and Test** — verification-oriented workflows that add tests for meaningful behavior or regression risk, use focused characterization checks when needed, and report blocked required checks as unverified.
- **Design** — Mirket's current published design-director skill for product UI, websites, illustration, brand systems, motion, slides, and generative artwork. It provides concise entry guidance and routes work to ten focused references, including interaction and content guidance and motion-and-gestures guidance covering timing, interruption, reduced motion, alternate controls, and safe removal. The current package is not the older five-stage `design-*` workflow described by stale knowledge documentation.
- **Mirket Audit** — the audit and lifecycle workflow distinguishes confirmed defects, supported risks, and material improvements, preserves read-only defaults, and requires authorization before fixes.
- **Mirket Clean** — the cleanup workflow. It performs quick applicability checks, scopes cleanup, preserves uncertain files, corrects guidance using evidence, and requires verified recovery copies before authorized removal.
- **Secure** — owns security and privacy work.
- **Release** — prepares versioned releases.
- **Migrate** — changes persistent state.
- **Deploy** — rolls out releases.
- **Operate** — maintains service health and recovery.
- **Focus** — includes a shipped-outcome review branch.
- **Mirket website** — the repository's separate static documentation and discovery project at `skills.mirket.dev`, created to explain and improve access to the Mirket plugin. It includes a compact skill index and workflow diagrams grounded in the current plugin documentation.
- **Hooks and hook trust review** — Mirket's configured hooks reinforce routing and communication guidance, cleanup, supported-commit acknowledgment, staged `.work` inspection, planning, and design checks. User-prompt handling routes communication guidance through Distill, while Stop and Bash pre-tool handling routes cleanup and related guardrails through cleanup logic. Hooks cannot guarantee model compliance, are not a complete shell parser or security boundary, and newly discovered hooks therefore require an explicit trust review.

The project vocabulary now includes Mirket's distributable skill catalog and package structure, its marketplace package, named routing and execution workflows, the root-agent/subagent orchestration model, persistent planning and independent review, the distinction between execution authorization and written-plan approval, Critique, Audit, Clean, Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, Operate, and verification workflows, the Mirket website and its source-backed documentation model, hook trust boundaries, project isolation, project-bank mapping, and memory continuity through Hindsight. The current package is version 0.4.0 with 25 composable workflows. Historical 43-skill, 20-current-skill, and 18-upstream-linked-parent-skill views remain separate catalog views and should not be treated as interchangeable.

- **Mirket website information architecture** — packaged skill metadata powers homepage cards, and each `SKILL.md` powers a corresponding skill-detail page. The site generates a static export in `website/out`.

- **Repository-sourced documentation** — the website documentation page uses repository Markdown as its source, so Mirket guidance is represented consistently in the repository, GitHub documentation, and the website.

- **Mirket website navigation model** — the source-backed site provides shared navigation with a sidebar, section links, and a skill index; skill pages link to adjacent skills and include breadcrumbs plus previous/next navigation. It also exposes keyboard skip navigation and a mobile skill index.

- **Website workflow diagram model** — the Mirket website's workflow diagram is separate from the packaged skills. Its ordered stages, labels, and glyphs are sourced from `workflows.json`, so the diagram is a presentation model of the workflow rather than another skill package.

- **Mirket lifecycle hooks** — host-invoked scripts distinct from packaged skills. They provide prompt guidance, route routine communication toward Distill, request cleanup review before delivery, and guard a defined subset of direct agent-shell Git commits; their behavior depends on host support and hook trust. The Codex plugin descriptor points to `hooks/hooks.json`; lifecycle events invoke `distill.py` or `cleanup.py`, which return JSON for the host to interpret and diagnose malformed or unsupported input. UserPromptSubmit emits Distill and Clean guidance, while Stop cleanup can request one continuation through the host's `stop_hook_active` flag. Hooks cannot guarantee model compliance, are not a complete shell parser or security boundary, and newly discovered hooks therefore require an explicit trust review.

- **Hindsight doctor** — reports daemon health, conversation coverage, survey findings, and page freshness as separate measurements.

- **Mirket Audit scope model** — Audit covers changes, plans, and systems or repositories explicitly included in scope. It should inspect manageable repositories completely and use a defensible risk-based scope for large repositories; it distinguishes confirmed defects, supported risks, and material improvements, and only corrects findings when the request or prior instructions authorize corrections.

- **Website content pipeline** — at build time, `website/lib/content.ts` reads the repository guide and packaged skill sources, including display metadata. The `app/` pages, reusable `components/`, and `lib/` content-loading code form the website project structure.

- **Equip's good-fit assessment** — as of 10 November 2026, Equip does more than help select or acquire tools: it critiques both the problem-solving approach and the instruments even when they work, distinguishes a working tool from a good-fit tool, identifies unnecessary cost, risk, constraints, inefficiency, or poor data correctness, explains the practical consequence, recommends a better fit, and gathers evidence. Its 13 user-approved discussion scenarios cover tool selection before a method exists, evidence gaps, fragile workflows, repeated workarounds, unavailable tools and fallbacks, authorized setup and first verification, hidden privacy or security costs, and deciding whether failure warrants replacement; they also include cases where keeping the current choice is best. Examples include preferring CSV or compact JSON over an inferior transfer format such as XLSX, avoiding floating-point values for financial records, rejecting an opinionated tool for a highly custom solution, and choosing a cleaner, more efficient library when the current one is materially inferior.

- **Mirket packaging manifests** — JSON manifests describe package contents and register Mirket's lifecycle hooks, complementing the Markdown workflows with YAML metadata and the distribution package structure.

- **RepoMarkdown** — the Mirket website's source-link mapping abstraction, which turns internal repository documentation links into website routes or GitHub links so repository-sourced documentation remains navigable in both contexts.

- **Mirket marketplace** — the project's marketplace distribution surface, named plainly `mirket`. It supports remote setup and includes a Mirket icon plus local workspace rules.

- **Equip representative-task check** — before or during authorized tool setup or change, Equip requires verification on a representative task. Its keep, adjust, pilot, or switch assessment weighs demonstrated downside against migration, compatibility, retraining, and ongoing ownership costs, while preserving human control.

- **Imagine** — a Mirket design-related destination workflow. Design sends Imagine only interface references, while retaining poster and identity references within Design's own scope.

- **Skill redesign baseline** — Mirket skill redesigns preserve existing authored work, reconcile shared guidance, and make the prior behavior visible as a baseline before changes are evaluated.

- **Hindsight doctor** — reports daemon health, conversation coverage, survey findings, and page freshness as separate measurements.

- **Pre-commit hook inspection model** — Mirket skills preserve quoted commit arguments and use a trusted Git probe for staged-index checks.

- **Mirket outcome routing** — each outcome has one responsible skill; supporting skills return evidence to that owner. This replaces the earlier parent-skill pattern in which parent skills routed each task to a relevant subskill, and clarifies responsibility across the current skill catalog.

- **Mirket plugin source layout** — the distributable `plugins/mirket/` package contains `plugin.json` for Codex metadata, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` for Claude metadata, `skills/` for the workflow catalog, `references/` for shared references, `assets/` for branding, and `hooks/` for Python lifecycle integrations. Skills use lowercase slugs under `plugins/mirket/skills/<slug>/`, with `SKILL.md` YAML front matter defining the trigger and description and `agents/openai.yaml` providing display metadata. Both plugin manifests identify version 0.4.0 and the package documents 25 workflows.

- **Distill operating model** — Mirket's Distill workflow favors authorized action over narration, reports concise factual progress and final technical outcomes with relevant checks and material limits, and directly challenges concerns with evidence and a recommendation while reducing avoidable communication overhead.

- **Architecture decision records (ADRs)** — settled architectural decisions in Mirket are stored under `docs/decisions/`; the Architect skill creates that directory for the first settled ADR when needed. `.work/decisions/` is reserved for private notes and drafts, not accepted decisions.

- **Workflow data model and diagram pipeline** — the website keeps one JSON workflow model for its animated presentation and checked-in SVG output. `data/workflows.json` feeds the workflow component and the diagram-generation script, which writes SVG diagrams under `docs/diagrams/`; this is a presentation model of the workflows, not another skill package.

- **Website discovery model** — `website/lib/content.ts` discovers lowercase packaged skill directories and builds records from each skill's Markdown and `agents/openai.yaml` metadata. `lib/discovery.ts` centralizes metadata and public-page discovery, while generated `/docs/skills/<slug>/` routes constrain skill pages to known packaged slugs. The site therefore consumes the package as its catalog source instead of maintaining a separate catalog.

Mirket is the only repository/project represented by the retrieved project-specific decisions. Mirket also uses a locally implemented static documentation website with compact pixel-art visuals, explanatory diagrams, responsive layouts, and system reduced-motion behavior. Its durable decisions emphasize explicit authorization distinct from approval of a written plan, preservation of authored work during skill redesign, risk-proportional review, reliable and diagnosable routing and recall, defensible lifecycle checks with opt-in final review, execution over routine narration, simplified onboarding and licensing, and evidence-based evaluation of tools and workflows. Its 25-skill catalog assigns distinct ownership across security, release, deployment, migration, service operations, and shipped-outcome review. Settled architectural decisions are recorded in the repository’s `docs/decisions/` directory, while `.work/decisions/` is reserved for private notes and drafts.

## Mirket — workflow architecture and enforcement boundary

- **Distribute Mirket as one composable collection of agent workflows.** Mirket is the repository’s primary plugin offering, with portable and host-specific manifests, `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` definitions, shared references, display metadata, an icon, and attribution notices. The rationale is to provide a coherent catalog whose workflows can be composed while preserving the packaging and metadata needed by each supported host.

- **Consolidate onboarding and licensing around a simple repository-owned entry point.** Mirket simplified and consolidated onboarding and its MIT licensing presentation. The rationale is to reduce adoption friction while making the project’s usage and redistribution terms clear.

- **Author skill guidance from Mirket’s own requirements and observed behavior.** Contributions must use original, native Mirket guidance rather than external skills, prompts, or workflow guides as authoring sources, while the root and packaged MIT license notices remain unchanged. This keeps the behavior contract owned by Mirket instead of importing assumptions from another codebase.

- **Give lifecycle skills distinct ownership boundaries.** Secure handles security and privacy, Release prepares versioned releases, Migrate changes persistent state, Deploy rolls releases out, and Operate maintains service health and recovery; Focus reviews shipped outcomes. This prevents overlapping responsibility and makes the Release → Deploy → Operate → Focus lifecycle explicit.

## Mirket — planning, authorization, and architecture

- **Require independent review for substantial plans without making unavailability a hidden stop.** Plan requests independent review and reports when it is unavailable; the agent’s own review must be labeled a “self-check,” not independent review. Execution does not automatically block solely because a reviewer is unavailable. This maintains independent scrutiny where valuable without falsely equating self-review with independence or preventing authorized work from proceeding.
- **Separate authorization to execute from approval of a written plan.** Clear existing authorization to execute remains valid and does not mean that an unapproved written plan is approved. Stronger approval gates still apply when the request is for a plan or approval is otherwise required. During execution, Plan asks about changes to outcomes, product decisions, or authorized scope, while routine regression checks do not become approval gates merely because planning guidance applies. This preserves authorized momentum without weakening explicit plan or scope decisions.
- **Use compact plans for small work and preserve structured records for substantial work.** Plan may use a compact plan for small tasks, while substantial work retains the project’s three `.work` plan records. This keeps lightweight work from acquiring needless process while preserving durable coordination records when the work warrants them.
- **Use Architect for consequential technical choices, not routine implementation.** Architect applies to substantial technical decisions and explicit architecture requests across new and existing systems. Decisions with material product, cost, security, or operations impact go to the user; routine choices remain within existing authorization. Research external options or patterns only when they could materially change the choice. This focuses architectural effort and human escalation on decisions that can materially alter outcomes. Plan and Equip approval gates likewise apply to changed acceptance criteria or material tool changes, not routine work.
- **Record settled architectural decisions in the repository’s `docs/decisions/` directory.** Architect initializes that directory for the first settled ADR when it does not exist; `.work/decisions/` is reserved for private notes and drafts. Diagrams are used when they clarify boundaries, flows, or trade-offs. This makes accepted decisions discoverable in the project while keeping provisional work separate. (REF-ID: `conversation:01a1c517-3c3f-7313-8a93-2858baddff8c`.)

- **Evaluate working choices by fit, not merely by whether they function.** Mirket Equip proactively challenges materially poor choices of tools, formats, representations, libraries, abstractions, and workflows, including choices that technically work. It gathers evidence about the downside, compares staying, adjusting, piloting, or switching against the expected benefit and adoption cost, and includes cases where keeping the current choice is best. This improves decision quality without removing human control; material changes still require specific authorization, and authorized setup is validated with a representative task because installation alone does not prove fit. The approved fit-scenario set is retained as a reference for these evaluations.

- **Preserve authored work and establish a visible baseline when redesigning skills.** Mirket skill redesigns reconcile shared guidance with existing authored work rather than silently replacing it, and show a visible baseline for comparison. This keeps intentional project-specific adaptations intact while making redesign effects reviewable.

- **Extend known comparisons only when the comparison is material and in scope.** Curate expands an existing comparison rather than broadening it opportunistically, and only when the additional comparison could materially affect the in-scope decision. This keeps evaluation useful without turning every task into an open-ended research exercise.

## Mirket — orchestration and delegation

- **Delegate only when it adds value; retain coordination at the root.** The root agent is the sole delegator and manager of delegated work; subagents cannot create or manage further subagents. Workers implement and provide evidence, then return ownership; the root may make bounded integration fixes after ownership returns while retaining any required independent review. This preserves clear responsibility for coordination without making workers perform every integration change. (REF-ID: `conversation:01a1c517-3c3f-7313-8a93-2858baddff8c`.)
- **Match capability and effort to determinism, creativity, risk, and ambiguity.** Use the fastest, least powerful suitable model for confident deterministic, rule-driven work; use a strong model with generous reasoning for creative work such as design, and ensure capability/reasoning is sufficient for high-risk or ambiguous tasks. This preserves quality where judgment is required while consistently controlling cost for work whose outcome is predictable. (REF-ID: `conversation:01a1bb84-4822-7903-a68a-ab67584fa15c`.)
- **Inspect outputs according to risk and return corrections to workers.** Results and evidence are checked in proportion to risk. Deficient work is returned to its worker or assigned to another worker, then rechecked. The rationale is that delegation does not transfer quality accountability away from the root. (REF-ID: `conversation:01a1bb84-4822-7903-a68a-ab67584fa15c`.)
- **Continue inline transparently when delegation is unavailable.** If subagents are unavailable, work continues inline with clear disclosure, and any unmet independent-review requirement remains explicit. Inline work is not independent review. This avoids unnecessary interruption while preserving an accurate record of assurance gaps. (REF-ID: `conversation:01a1bb84-4822-7903-a68a-ab67584fa15c`.)

## Mirket — review, testing, investigation, and cleanup

- **Make lifecycle checks conservative about repository state and explicit about command semantics.** Mirket’s pre-commit protection uses a trusted Git probe with an absolute `git -C` target for read-only staged-index inspection, disables external helpers during that inspection, preserves quoted punctuation when recognizing compound commands, and handles commit modes such as `git commit -a` and path-based commits whose file sets differ from the current index. `git commit --dry-run` previews remain read-only. Recognized commit commands run separately from other shell commands so earlier commands cannot change the inspected target index. It blocks when the target index cannot be inspected, allowing only one exact, explicitly authorized path exception. This prevents false approvals and false blocks caused by shell parsing, command sequencing, or by assuming that the current index always represents the commit.

- **Keep cleanup responsibility explicit while making final review opt-in.** Mirket’s cleanup hook is Stop-neutral by default and activates extra final-review behavior only when `MIRKET_FINAL_REVIEW=1`; when opt-in is enabled and `stop_hook_active` is false, it can request continuation. A neutral hook result does not authorize skipping cleanup. This avoids an unnecessary model pass for every response while preserving an explicit way to request final review when needed.

- **Make Author and Distill serve communication without turning routine replies into documents.** Distill handles routine responses, while Author applies to user-facing replies as well as documents, substantive copy, and issue triage through a lightweight combined pass. The pass adapts audience and format to context, asks when that choice could materially change the result, verifies material claims and artifacts according to risk, and labels uncertainty when verification is not possible. This favors authorized action and concise, accurate communication without claiming that advisory guidance guarantees compliance; any additional final review is separately opt-in through `MIRKET_FINAL_REVIEW=1`.

- **Defer live skill evaluation until lifecycle-hook changes are ready.** Mirket’s lifecycle-hook work postpones live skill evaluation while the hooks and related safety changes are still being revised. This avoids treating an in-progress lifecycle design as a stable basis for evaluation.

- **Validate source, package, installation, and host behavior together.** Mirket treats synchronization between repository source, packaged contents, copied global instructions, installed skill guidance, and hook trust state as a release concern; validating the package alone is insufficient. Audits also distinguish pre-existing working-tree changes from released or installed state, and local tests are not presented as proof of fresh-host activation or live semantic routing. This prevents repository findings and static test success from being mistaken for verified deployed behavior.

## Mirket — pre-commit protection and command recognition

## Mirket — routing, research, handoff, and communication

- **Use a canonical project registry as the single source of truth for project-specific routing and recall, with one owner per outcome.** Mirket assigns each outcome to one responsible skill; supporting skills return evidence to that skill rather than adding a router to every request. The registry unifies routing for Codex hooks, interactive MCP, surveys, and background collection; canonical Git project directories make subdirectories and linked worktrees resolve to the owning project bank, while non-Git sessions retain their original directory and unrelated repositories with the same basename are rejected. The guarded survey adapter uses the same resolver as hooks and interactive MCP and refuses writes when the resolved bank differs. Read-only audits do not start execution plans. Session bindings can be recovered from verified transcript metadata when temporary markers are absent, and setup and rewiring are reproducible. Page-first injection supplies fast current context while verified transcript recovery provides source recall; legacy banks are preserved and eligible history is reconciled non-destructively. A doctor checks routing, host wiring, coverage, page freshness, targeted recall, and daemon health separately so a working installation is not mistaken for complete or current recall.

- **Pass only the interface needed across Design and Imagine handoffs.** Mirket sends interface references rather than unnecessary internal detail from Design to Imagine.

- **Treat memory configuration and project identity as reliability boundaries.** Mirket’s memory work preserves existing working-tree revisions while fixing configuration preservation, canonical bank migration, effective diagnostics, and explicit freshness and recovery checks. Rewiring must preserve effective upstream capture and environment settings or reject customized registrations; legacy linked-worktree mappings must resolve through the canonical project identity rather than silently creating a new bank; and diagnostics must use the same effective configuration as runtime execution. This prevents split recall, accidental capture-policy changes, and false confidence from a healthy-looking but mis-targeted diagnostic.

- **Preserve supplied-mockup routing in Design.** When a supplied mockup determines the design input, Design keeps that routing rather than replacing it with a generic design path. This preserves the user-provided source of visual truth while retaining the project’s explicit handoff boundaries.

## Mirket — documentation website and visual system

- **Explain the plugin through a local static Next.js documentation site.** Mirket’s site is implemented under `website/` and produces a static export for `skills.mirket.dev`, making working principles, installation, and the full catalog easier to understand across devices.
- **Use repository Markdown and packaged metadata as the documentation source of truth.** The repository guide is rendered on the site, packaged skill metadata supplies homepage cards, and each `SKILL.md` supplies its detail page. `RepoMarkdown` maps internal source links to site routes or GitHub, keeping references usable in both contexts. Keyboard skip navigation and a mobile index keep the same source-backed documentation discoverable on GitHub and the site.
- **Make installation the stable entry point.** The homepage replaces a hero animation panel with copyable agent prompts and manual installation commands for Codex and Claude Code, while retaining the workflow diagrams below; this keeps the first interaction practical and reproducible. Installer selections use a stable 390px height so switching hosts does not cause layout shifts, and the hero description uses terminal-style monospace to reinforce the installation-oriented presentation.
- **Use a compact retro pixel-art visual system.** The site uses the normal Mirket logo in the header, footer, and favicon, plus a darker true pixel-art meerkat with clear edges, confident posture, expressive eyes, original fur markings, and three-quarter proportions. The still 64×64 sprite is settled before further animation decisions so animation does not drive an unapproved asset.
- **Use explanatory diagrams and responsive interaction instead of text alone.** The compact diagrams resolve mobile label sizing, and the mascot can react to nearby controls and wave or wink after pointer, touch, or keyboard activation. Static-build and desktop/mobile checks down to 320px passed. The homepage section is titled “How it Works”; playback follows the system preference.
- **Honor the system reduced-motion preference site-wide.** Reduced motion is controlled by the browser/system setting rather than a page-level control; the mascot stays still and shows a heart instead of animated movement, and diagrams remain still. This preserves communication and character while respecting accessibility preferences.
- **Make the documentation discoverable beyond direct browsing.** Mirket documents all 25 skills across 23 pages, with unique metadata and canonical URLs, structured data, `llms.txt`, a sitemap, robots directives, and page-specific Open Graph and X preview images. These repository-owned outputs improve search, answer-engine, crawler, and social-preview access without creating a second source of truth.

- **Use one workflow data source for interactive and generated documentation views.** `website/data/workflows.json` drives both the browser workflow player and the Node-generated SVG diagrams checked into `docs/diagrams/`. This avoids maintaining divergent workflow definitions while keeping the site’s interactive explanation and repository documentation aligned.
